what.text: Pyrilutamide (KX-826) is an androgen receptor blocker put on the scalp as a solution (tincture). It is being developed by Suzhou Kintor Pharmaceutical in China for male and female androgenetic alopecia. A 2026 review describes it as aiming to block the androgen receptor in the scalp without lowering hormones in the body.
Chemists have used it as the comparison drug when testing newer topical androgen receptor blockers in mice.

src.label: Zhang et al., J Med Chem

what.text: No peer-reviewed results from any pyrilutamide trial were found as of November 1, 2026.

research.text: Seven KX-826 trials are registered on ClinicalTrials.gov: two Phase 1, three Phase 2, one Phase 3 and one Phase 2/3. Six are sponsored by Suzhou Kintor and one by Suzhou Koshine Biomedica. None has posted results, and no journal paper reporting their results was found.
A PubMed search for 'pyrilutamide' returned 3 records and one for 'KX-826' returned 1; none reports trial results. ClinicalTrials.gov lists 7 KX-826 trials.

research.found: The registry status is 'unknown' (last verified November 2023). No results are posted. A new Phase 2/3 trial of 0.5% and 1.0% solution in 756 Chinese men was registered in 2024 as not yet recruiting.

us.text: Pyrilutamide is not FDA approved for any use. It has been tested in US Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials. Any product sold outside a trial is an unapproved drug. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: FDA's drug database has no product containing pyrilutamide. Unapproved drugs have not been reviewed by FDA for safety, effectiveness or quality.
two Phase 1 trials (2019, 2020) and one Phase 2 trial in 123 men (2022 to 2023) were run in the US.

FDA has said that companies selling unapproved drugs labelled “for research purposes” or “not for human consumption” directly to consumers for human use did so illegally. That statement was about GLP-1 drugs; FDA has not issued one naming pyrilutamide.

world.lead: Pyrilutamide is an investigational drug. No approval was found in the US, Canada or the EU. Its late-stage trials are in China. It is not named on WADA’s list. WADA’s class for unapproved drugs (S0) may cover it, but WADA has not said so.

after.text: Pyrilutamide is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. The lists' class S0 bans, at all times, any pharmacological substance not covered by another class that has no current approval by any government health authority for human therapeutic use, including drugs in development or discontinued. No such approval was found for Pyrilutamide, so that class’s wording may cover it. WADA has not ruled on it.

side.text: No safety results from pyrilutamide trials have been posted or published. Its side effects in people are not publicly known.

items.text: the Phase 1 trials measured side effects and skin irritation, but no results are posted.
as an androgen receptor blocker, it is being tested in both men and women; no trial result on hormone or sexual side effects was found.

unconfirmed: Company announcements about KX-826 trial results were not reviewed; only registry and journal records were used, and neither holds results.
Pyrilutamide's status with China's NMPA (including any marketing application) was not checked.
The outcome of the 740-man Chinese Phase 3 trial (NCT06126965) is not posted; its registry status is 'unknown'.
UK and Australian status were not checked against a regulator record.
surprises: Pyrilutamide has been through seven registered trials since 2019, including a 740-man Phase 3, yet none has posted results or a peer-reviewed paper as of November 1, 2026.
